parsed.attack: A streak is the wrong mechanic for this behaviour: private practice happens when a parent is free and the car is available, which is once or twice a week, so 'a visible unbroken run of days' is mathematically broken by Wednesday of week one and the core loop discredits itself before the habit forms. And the UK, unlike New South Wales or Victoria, mandates no logged hours - no examiner, DVSA form or insurer ever asks to see this record, so nothing outside the app consumes the artifact and the logging is pure self-motivation for a seventeen-year-old. The whole thing then terminates absolutely on test day: pass, and the log, the streak and the account are dead the same afternoon, with no second product to sell the same person.
parsed.strongest_defence: A one-time purchase is settled before any of that matters, and for the six months of learning the return trigger is genuinely every drive - the countersigning parent is a second human enforcing it, which is stronger than a streak and is why the invite is for function rather than growth. The record has an external consumer if you point it at one: the paid instructor, who currently has no visibility of what happened between lessons and can price and plan against it, and 'hours before test' is a number learners and parents both already track in their heads.
parsed.verdict_reason: There is a real reason to open it after each practice drive, but the daily-streak mechanic is mismatched with a weekly behaviour and no institution demands the record, so the habit lock the moat depends on never engages.
